column3: The PolyC BootstrapCalcPadding and the C CalcPadding are run side-by-side on a corpus of (offset, size) pairs; any divergence flips rc.
Production delegation (parseClassOffsets / parseUnionOffsets routing to the PolyC component) is reserved for the next-next ACT; this ACT only ADDS the PolyC component and the differential oracle.
tools/bootstrap/selfhost-parser-padding.HC compiles and links as a standalone translation unit; a tiny HC driver loops over the corpus and exits 0.
The PolyC source is committed in tools/bootstrap/ (not generated at build time); the build artifact is reproducible from source + toolchain.
A stub mutation harness applies each of Class A-D (per c2-selected-red-contract.txt) to the PolyC component and confirms the oracle flags it.
CalcPadding is a 2-input primitive; a finite, mechanically-generated corpus of (offset, size) pairs covering the partition is the equivalent of "broad corpus" for this subject.
LEXER01..04 fixtures must continue to PASS unchanged; this ACT does not touch any lexer source.
parseClassOffsets / parseUnionOffsets output must be byte-identical before and after the ACT (production change is zero).
git diff --check on the closure range must be clean.
The terminal-verdict tooling (oracle) is implemented in PolyC (HC); shell wrappers <=50 LOC dispatch only.
No Python sources, no Python invocations, no Python fallback.
No modification of any closed evidence or HANDOFF (LEXER01..04, SURFACE-RECON03, PARSER01, PARSER01-CORRECTION01).
